A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CS-Aligner. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and rendered figures, support reliable comparison despite reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V2 reports original text-to-image generation, image-text retrieval, few-shot classification, and ablation results.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds captioning, divergence comparisons, and retrieval analyses.

M1.justification: The CS-plus-InfoNCE objective, estimator, token alignment, and adapter/LoRA procedures remain unchanged. Appendix H adds a task-specific captioning adaptation: a BLIP-2-style Q-former trained with InfoNCE, language-model loss, and CS divergence, as shown in Table 6.

E1.justification: V3 adds image captioning on MSCOCO, introducing image-to-text generation beyond v2's generation, retrieval, and classification coverage. Appendix H.1 also introduces MSCOCO retrieval evaluation. The earlier training datasets and benchmark coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds SD v2.1, SD-unclip v2.1, Wurstchen, and IB with the Kandinsky decoder. Appendix D.4 adds a quantitative comparison involving Gaussian KL, Gaussian Wasserstein, and Sinkhorn; v2 only evaluated unpaired KL failure and discussed Wasserstein. Captioning also introduces an InfoNCE+LM control.

E3.justification: Existing experimental settings are retained. Added experiments introduce an SD-unclip decoder configuration, BLIP-2-style captioning evaluated with BLEU-1/CIDEr, and retrieval sensitivity measured with R@1. Appendix D.4 specifies Gaussian batch-embedding assumptions for tractable KL/Wasserstein comparisons and a Sinkhorn alternative.

E4.justification: V3 substantially broadens tests of the CS component through quantitative divergence alternatives in Appendix D.4, retrieval hyperparameter sensitivity in Table 8, and retrieval loss ablations in Table 9. The earlier generation sensitivity, token, unpaired-data, multiple-caption, and adaptation analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V3's discussion of variance and a central limit theorem concerns theoretical estimator stability, rather than uncertainty reporting for experimental results.

E6.justification: Retained scores are unchanged, but substantial results are added. Table 1 reports FID 10.88 for CS-Aligner with SD-unclip and 150.52 for IB with Kandinsky. Appendix D.4 reports KL 23.48, Wasserstein 18.41, CS-Aligner 12.62, and Sinkhorn nonconvergence. Captioning BLEU-1/CIDEr are 40.4/14.3 without CS and 41.3/16.7 with CS; Table 9 adds retrieval averages of 57.95 versus 58.52.

T1.justification: New Appendix E adds mathematical stability reasoning using spherical distance concentration, O(1/sqrt(d)) fluctuations, the condition nσ^d much greater than 1, and a KDE central-limit argument. It also states O(N²) computational complexity. Existing toy-example calculations and InfoNCE/CS derivations are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: combining distributional CS alignment with InfoNCE, addressing alignment–uniformity conflict, and exploiting unpaired samples and tokens. The added experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations of excessive λ, temperature-related generation failure, and why retrieval can succeed without full distributional overlap. It explicitly frames generation as an alignment proxy and adds stability/scalability interpretations. V2's limitations/future-work paragraph concerning generation architectures and broader modalities is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix G.1 newly documents Figure 1's adapter comparison, MSCOCO training, 5K validation pairs, t-SNE, distance histogram, and CLIP-initialized learnable temperature. Appendix H.1 also discloses temperature handling for the retained generation ablation. Existing hardware, optimizer, learning rate, architecture, and decoder details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds references to the IB alignment method, BLIP-2, Wurstchen, and concentration-of-measure theory, while dropping the MiniGPT-4/chatbot example. The CS-divergence related-work passage moves from Section 5 to Appendix C with its research positioning preserved.

P1.justification: V3 makes local language refinements and merges the adapter/LoRA explanations. It relocates CS related work and broader impacts, adds LLM-use and reproducibility statements, and groups supplementary ablations under H.1. Most of the main narrative and method exposition remain closely matched.

P2.justification: V3 adopts ICLR title, header, heading, and page formatting throughout. It expands Table 1, restructures the loss-ablation table to combine retrieval and generation, and adds divergence, captioning, and retrieval-sensitivity tables plus Figure 8. Figures 1–7 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: Direct divergence comparisons and retrieval ablations strengthen evidence for the central CS-alignment mechanism, while Figure 1 and temperature disclosures improve reproducibility. Captioning adds useful applicability evidence. These gains are limited by incomplete protocol details for new experiments, the brief support for strong stability guarantees in Appendix E, and removal of the explicit limitations paragraph.
